description.text: ADS is the leading manufacturer of innovative water management solutions in the stormwater and onsite wastewater industries, providing superior drainage solutions to manage the world’s most precious resource: water. Our innovative products are used across a broad range of end markets and applications, including residential, non-residential, infrastructure and agriculture applications. We have established a leading position in many of these end markets by leveraging our national sales and distribution platform, market share model, industry-acclaimed engineering support, overall product breadth and scale plus manufacturing excellence. Our best-in-class product portfolio, go-to-market strategy and material conversion strategy helped drive consistent above market growth. On February 2, 2026, we completed the acquisition of National Diversified Sales (“NDS”). NDS is a leading designer and manufacturer of residential stormwater and drainage solutions focused on managing surface and subsurface water around homes. NDS develops durable, easy-to-install products that help homeowners and contractors control runoff, prevent water damage, and protect landscapes and foundations. This combination brings together complementary water management solutions to expand our offerings.

analysis_md:
# WMS — Advanced Drainage Systems, Inc.
Pass-1 run, 2026-10-20 (engine release 5.5.0). All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, financials_history.csv or fundamentals.json — none are recomputed.

## What it is
North America's leading water-management products maker: corrugated HDPE pipe and stormwater systems, Infiltrator septic/leachfield chambers, plus the acquired Orenco (FY2025) and NDS (closed February 2026) product lines, reorganized after NDS into Stormwater and Wastewater segments. Sales split across non-residential, residential, infrastructure and agriculture construction end markets. Price $127.78 (nasdaq_quote_api); market cap $10.016B — in scope (under $40B).

## Owner's earnings
**FY2026 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $819,054,000; capex $249,766,000 (tag: PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment, rollup, every year filed — no coverage gap); SBC $32,354,000 (AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense; always a real cost).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2026: $536,934,000 = $6.85/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE total $536.9M, latest FY OE/share $6.85).
- Maintenance version FY2026 (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC, from financials_history.csv): $391,185,000 — below the conservative figure because FY2026 net income carried NDS acquisition and restructuring costs (Q4 FY2026 net income from continuing operations fell 54.1% YoY on those costs per the company's release) while the OCF-based figure is not burdened the same way. The conservative OCF-based series is the one used throughout.
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years. OE/share by year: FY2022 $1.39, FY2023 $6.23, FY2024 $6.35, FY2025 $4.37, FY2026 $6.85 (financials_history.csv) — the FY2022 trough was a working-capital and resin-margin year (OCF fell to $274,888,000), the FY2025 dip a working-capital build year (OCF $581,491,000).
- **Base used = normalized: median of the last 3 FY OE/share = $6.35/share** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share). No STALE_FY flag (FY ended 2026-03-31, 6.7 months ago) and no BASE_DIVERGENCE flag — latest FY $6.85 sits close to the median, so no TTM pin is needed; for reference the fundamentals.json TTM through Q1 FY2027 (2026-06-30) prints OE/share $6.57, between the two, which supports the median as the base rather than a distortion.
- **Discontinued operations (checked, statements.json):** the income statement reports discontinued operations of $0 in FY2024, $0 in FY2025 and a $1,090,000 loss in FY2026. The median year (FY2024) contains none, and even if the entire FY2026 loss had been cash inside OCF it amounts to $0.014/share against FY2026 OE/share of $6.85 (0.2%) — a continuing-operations rebuild cannot move the $6.35 median base or the tier. The $5,653,000 Q1 FY2027 discontinued-operations loss sits outside the annual base window, and no TTM base is used.
- Net debt $1.389B (key_numbers.md), 2.79x normalized OE — up after funding NDS (~$991M cash, February 2026) largely from cash on hand plus a new term loan; lease liabilities a further $74.2M (dcf_numbers.json). No HIGH_NET_DEBT flag at this level, but leverage is no longer the near-zero of the pre-deal balance sheet.

## Moat: 6/10 — moderate-strong
Justification: North America's leading stormwater manager with scale in corrugated HDPE pipe, a dense local plant/distribution network that confers a freight-cost advantage on bulky pipe, Infiltrator's dominant plastic leachfield-chamber position, spec/code approvals and one of the largest plastic-recycling operations in North America (resin-cost integration) — against a near-commodity core product, resin/freight cost squeezes and construction cyclicality.
- FOR: #1 North American stormwater position and the broadest water-management product line (pipe, chambers, Infiltrator, NDS, Orenco); 60+ local plants — freight is the binding cost on bulky, low value-density pipe, so local density is a structural cost advantage smaller rivals cannot match; spec-in/code-approval position with engineers and distributors defaulting to ADS systems; recycled-resin vertical integration.
- AGAINST: JM Eagle, Lane Enterprises and regional makers plus concrete/steel pipe substitution contest every bid — the product itself is close to commodity; resin and transportation inflation compresses margin before pricing catches up; demand is construction-cyclical with no recurring-revenue lock-in; growth is increasingly bought (NDS, Orenco), adding goodwill, integration risk and debt.
- Evidence (fundamentals.json): ROIC proxy 17.6% (FY2021), 16.3% (FY2022), 29.3% (FY2023), 28.8% (FY2024), 21.5% (FY2025) — well above the cost of capital through a full resin cycle — easing to 14.5% in FY2026, when the ~$991M NDS deal closed one month before year-end and inflated invested capital ahead of its earnings. Gross margin: 34.8% → 28.9% (FY2022 resin squeeze) → 36.4% / 39.9% / 37.7% / 38.3% (FY2023–FY2026), 38.6% TTM — pricing power is real, but it arrives with a lag, which is why this is 6 and not higher.
- A 6 gives CAP = 9.8 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 9.8 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — final run (2026-10-20)
**Growth-start sanity check (mandatory):** the engine blend is 5.44% (rev CAGR 5y 9.00%, rev CAGR 3y -0.23%, latest rev YoY 5.03%, OE/share CAGR 2y 3.83%, plus the +2.02pp buyback adjustment on revenue components). Against the prints: FY2027 guidance (reaffirmed at Q1, 2026-08-06) is net sales $3.35–3.55B (+9.8% to +16.4% vs FY2026) but adjusted EBITDA only $1.00–1.05B vs $962.9M in FY2026 (+3.9% to +9.0%), with adjusted EBITDA margin guided down ~170–200bp on resin and transportation costs. The base start of 5.4% OE growth therefore sits mid-range of the company's own guided EBITDA growth — the sales guide is higher only because NDS annualizes and margins compress. Q1 FY2027 printed sales +20.6% YoY to $1.001B, but that includes $94.7M of NDS contribution, ~9.2% organic growth and $25–30M of customer pull-forward ahead of price increases — it is a revenue print, not an OE growth rate, and it does not make the bull start (10.4%) too low: bull OE growth of 10.4% already exceeds the top of guided FY2027 EBITDA growth (+9.0%) and so implicitly assumes NDS synergies/margin recovery beyond guidance. Super-bull 17.4% is a genuine tail (Investor Day targets >8% organic CAGR and >$1.2B EBITDA by FY2030). Bear 0.4% and super-bear -6.6% have direct precedent: FY2024 revenue fell 6.4% and FY2022 OE/share collapsed on resin costs. Probabilities 10/30/30/20/10 — bear widened from the 25% default per the OE_VOLATILE flag; OE multipliers at the 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25 defaults. Price $127.78.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | -6.6% | 0.75 | Construction downturn plus a FY2022-style resin squeeze; NDS synergies disappoint | $26.13 | 4.73% |
| Bear | 30% | 0.4% | 0.90 | Guided FY2027 margin compression persists; residential stays soft | $42.79 | 6.59% |
| Base | 30% | 5.4% | 1.00 | Guided EBITDA growth (~+4–9%) compounds; margins recover gradually post-FY2027 | $59.40 | 8.44% |
| Bull | 20% | 10.4% | 1.10 | NDS cross-selling lands, price increases stick, non-residential/data-center demand holds | $81.60 | 10.77% |
| Super bull | 10% | 17.4% | 1.25 | Investor-Day path delivered early: >8% organic CAGR with margin expansion | $126.39 | 14.88% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $62.23 (-51.3% vs price), IV@12% $83.15, IV@10% $106.56, weighted IRR 8.80%, base-case IRR 8.44%**
- **Tier by numbers: D.** Diagnostics (key_numbers.md): OE yield 4.97%, terminal value 19.4% of IV@15%, scenario spread 4.84x, net debt 2.79x normalized OE, 6.7 months since FY end.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **BUYBACK_TAILWIND** (share count shrinking 2.0%/yr): already credited via the +2.02pp growth adjustment in the blend; not double-counted in the verdict. Q1 FY2027 alone repurchased 1.6M shares for $228.5M — the shrink is real and funded from OCF.
- **OE_VOLATILE** (OE/share spans >3x over 5 years): real and explained — FY2022's $1.39/share was the resin-price spike (gross margin 28.9%) plus a working-capital outflow year, FY2025's $4.37 a working-capital build. Handled by the normalized median base ($6.35 vs latest $6.85) and by widening the bear probability to 30%.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (FY2026 net income vs OCF differ by >40%): resolved from the FY2026 10-K cash-flow statement (net income, D&A, SBC, deferred taxes and the working-capital lines per financials_history.csv / statements.json) — the gap is non-cash mechanics, not a one-off inflating OCF. Net income $426,465,000 reconciles to OCF $819,054,000 mainly via depreciation & amortization $216,261,000 (a real cost already charged to OE through capex of $249,766,000), deferred income taxes $35,228,000, stock compensation $32,354,000, loss on disposal/exit costs $19,211,000, and the non-cash NDS inventory step-up $12,277,000; the named working-capital lines net to only +$25,639,000 (accounts payable +$53,960,000 and receivables +$2,288,000, partly offset by a $30,609,000 inventory build), ~3% of OCF. The OCF-based base is trustworthy.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (super-bull IV 4.84x super-bear): real — the outcome range is genuinely wide for a cyclical at this price. Confidence is capped at medium, and the verdict is sized to the conservative end.
- **TIER_BAND** (bear tier D at 6.59% vs bull tier C at 10.77%): the verdict is sized to the bear end — both bear and base are Tier D, and even the super-bull case (14.88%) does not clear the 15% hurdle, so the band does not change the conclusion.

## My thoughts / overlay
- This is a quality-versus-price result, not a quality problem: ROIC in the high-teens to high-20s through the cycle, ~38% gross margins, OCF converting above net income, a real buyback, and a leading franchise — bought at a 4.97% OE yield with mid-single-digit guided earnings growth. At $127.78 the market is paying for the Investor-Day FY2030 story (>8% organic CAGR, >$1.2B EBITDA) today.
- The swing factors are all visible: FY2027 resin/freight margin pressure (guided), NDS integration and cross-selling (Q1 showed limited cross-selling so far), and whether residential construction recovers. None of them needs to go wrong for the stock to underperform the 15% hurdle — the base case already fails it.
- Leverage watch: net debt $1.389B (2.79x normalized OE) is manageable but new for ADS; buybacks at $127.78 are being executed well above the weighted IV@15% of $62.23, which destroys per-share value on this model even as they shrink the count.
- Method range: the verdict is robust, not assumption-dominated — preliminary run (defaults, moat 5) printed weighted IRR 8.85% / IV@15% $63.04, the final run 8.80% / $62.23, and no scenario in either run reaches 15%.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (weighted IRR 8.80%; bear D 6.59% → bull C 10.77%; clears 15% only below the weighted IV@15% of $62.23, 20% below $43.52, 25% below $33.28)
- Confidence: **Medium** (clean filed data, no gaps, no overrides; capped by the 4.84x scenario spread and OE cyclicality)
- One-liner: High-quality stormwater franchise, moat 6/10 with ROIC 16–29% through the cycle — but at $127.78 the OE yield is only 4.97% and weighted IRR is 8.80% (IV@15% $62.23); it clears 15% only below ~$62, and even the super-bull case (14.88%) stays under the hurdle.
